Research

Habitability and origin of life

Are we alone?

How do chemical origins shape planetary diversity and habitability across stellar environments? With a deeper understanding of the chemical diversity of rocky worlds, I would be excited to probe into the origin(s) and prevalence of life in the cosmos.

Publications

  • Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE) XIV. Finding terrestrial protoplanets in the galactic neighborhood
    L. Cesario, T. Lichtenberg, E. Alei, Ó. Carrión-González, F. A. Dannert, et al. (incl. H. S. Wang) (2024)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 692, A172 · DOI · arXiv
    Shows that LIFE could detect hot, young rocky protoplanets in their magma ocean epoch in stellar associations out to about 100 pc.
  • The Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE): A space mission for mid-infrared nulling interferometry
    A. M. Glauser, S. P. Quanz, et al. (incl. H. S. Wang) (2024)
    SPIE Optical and Infrared Interferometry and Imaging IX, 13095, 354–374
    Describes the LIFE space mission concept for mid-infrared nulling interferometry.
  • Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE): VIII. Where is the phosphine? Observing exoplanetary PH3 with a space based MIR nulling interferometer
    D. Angerhausen, M. Ottiger, F. Dannert, Y. Miguel, C. Sousa-Silva, J. Kammerer, F. Menti, E. Alei, B. S. Konrad, H. S. Wang, S. P. Quanz (2023)
    Astrobiology, 23, 183–184 · DOI · arXiv
    Assesses in which cases phosphine, a potential biosignature molecule, would be observable in exoplanet atmospheres with a mission like LIFE.
  • A model Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of α Centauri A/B
    H. S. Wang, C. H. Lineweaver, S. P. Quanz, S. J. Mojzsis, T. R. Ireland, P. A. Sossi, F. Seidler, T. Morel (2022)
    The Astrophysical Journal, 927, 134 · DOI · arXiv
    Predicts the bulk composition, interior structure and early atmosphere of a hypothetical Earth-sized planet in the habitable zone of the nearest binary system.
  • Large Interferometer For Exoplanets (LIFE)
    S. P. Quanz, M. Ottiger, E. Fontanet, J. Kammerer, et al. (incl. H. S. Wang) (2022)
    Astronomy & Astrophysics, 664, A21 · DOI · arXiv
    Estimates that a space-based mid-infrared nulling interferometer could detect hundreds of nearby exoplanets, including about 25–45 rocky planets in the empirical habitable zone of their host stars.
